clue.text: Take cases of Armagnac, champagne and port

indicators.note: the cases of each word are its outside letters, first and last, which hold the rest like a box

parts.note: outer letters A and C
outer letters C and E
outer letters P and T

explanation.surface: Someone takes delivery of crates of brandy, fizz and fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases' reads as boxes of drink, but here it means the outside letters of each of the three drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept something is to receive or agree to take it when offered.

clue.text: Corporation's oilman, bad rogue

definitions.note: corporation is humorous British slang for a pot belly, so of the corporation means of the belly, an adjective

indicators.note: rogue means behaving wildly or out of control, so the letters go astray

explanation.surface: A big company's oil executive turns out to be a bad lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a business, but in old British slang it is a large belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Abdominal means relating to the belly, which a paunch is jokingly called.

clue.text: Troops riding in white lorry regularly overlooked

parts.note: cava is a Spanish sparkling white wine

indicators.note: letters overlooked at regular intervals means alternate ones are skipped, keeping the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: Soldiers are carried in a white truck that is often ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavalry are soldiers who fight on horseback, mounted troops.

clue.text: Official border moving north over time is theft

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above, coming first
in a down answer moving north means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: ref is short for referee, a match official
a lip is a rim or border
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A frontier official heading north over a period is guilty of stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilferage is petty stealing, the taking of small items over time.

clue.text: Some Luddite man resumes turning handle on computer

indicators.note: turning signals that the concealed letters are read backwards
only some of the letters of the following words are used, so the answer sits inside them

parts.note: the hidden run spans the end of Luddite, all of man and most of resumes

explanation.surface: A technophobe goes back to fiddling with the knob on his machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handle' looks like a knob to grip, but it is the name you log in with. A Luddite is someone who opposes new technology.
explanation.definitionFit: Online, a handle is the alias or login identity a user goes by on a computer system.

clue.text: Relative's back home keeping company with us

indicators.note: keeping means the first pieces hold the others within them

parts.note: to second a motion is to back or support it
in means at home
taken as written

explanation.surface: A relation is back home living with the family company.
explanation.definitionFit: A second cousin is a kinsman who shares great-grandparents with you.

clue.text: Hammering head of rivet exposed

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: out means revealed or exposed, as a secret is out

explanation.surface: A rivet's head is left showing after the hammering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammering' looks like the act of driving in a rivet, but it means a heavy defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is a crushing defeat, which informally is called a hammering.

clue.text: Tree likely to bear fruit crop now and then

indicators.note: to bear means to carry, so the word for likely carries the other letters inside

parts.note: apt means likely, as in apt to fail

indicators.note: now and then means only occasional letters are taken, every other one

explanation.surface: An orchard tree looks set to produce a harvest from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Now and then' keeps the even-placed letters of 'fruit crop', and 'to bear' means the word for likely carries them.
explanation.definitionFit: The apricot is a small fruit tree with orange stone fruit.

clue.text: Around November, first of two journalists quit

indicators.note: around means letters are placed round the letter for November
first of means the letter goes into the first of the pair, not the second

parts.note: ED is an editor, so two journalists give two EDs
N is November in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: In November, the first of two reporters resigned.
explanation.walkthrough: The first ED goes around N, followed by the second ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Ended is a past tense meaning stopped, as quit can mean ceased.

clue.text: Son experienced returning terrors

indicators.note: returning means the joined letters are taken back the other way, read backwards

parts.note: lived, as in lived through something, means experienced

explanation.surface: A son who has been through a lot comes home to face his fears.
explanation.definitionFit: Little devils and terrors are both mischievous, troublesome children, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Got constant amount of paper across which to display advert

indicators.note: the advert is to be displayed spread across the paper, so its letters go round the other pieces

parts.note: C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
a quire is a set measure of paper, twenty-four or twenty-five sheets

explanation.surface: Someone obtained a fixed quantity of paper on which to print a newspaper advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: To have acquired something is to have got or obtained it.

clue.text: Losing interest with scoffing bananas

indicators.note: going bananas is going crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone eats bananas greedily but is bored with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like the food being scoffed, but it is slang for crazy, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Switching off is an idiom for ceasing to pay attention, becoming bored.

clue.text: Drunkenly wield menu collecting large drink

indicators.note: collecting means the rearranged letters gather another letter inside them
drunkenly suggests the letters of wield menu stagger into a new order

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A tipsy diner waves the menu about while picking up a big drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange WIELD MENU to MULEDWINE, then put L for large inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mulled wine is a hot spiced wine served as a warming winter beverage.

clue.text: Sour when caught dipping into charitable fund

indicators.note: dipping into means one piece goes inside another, as a hand dips into a purse

parts.note: aid is help given, here money raised for charity
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone turns bitter on being caught helping themselves from a charity's money.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid and sour both describe a sharp, tart taste, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Vote against entering area in New York

indicators.note: entering means the letter for area goes in between the letters of New York

explanation.surface: A local vote opposing some plan in a New York district.
explanation.definitionFit: A nay is a no vote, the opposite of an aye in a legislative division.

clue.text: Lorry delayed between American states

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry, a British truck with a separate cab and trailer

indicators.note: between means the word for delayed is placed between the two letters for American

parts.note: US stands for American, as in US forces
late means delayed

explanation.surface: A truck is held up while travelling from one US state to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American states' looks like a single phrase, but 'states' alone is the verb the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: To articulate a point is to express or put it into words clearly.

clue.text: Attempting to hear record, turning up good number

parts.note: to list something is to record it

indicators.note: in a down answer turning up means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: nine is a number

explanation.surface: Someone straining to hear a record while turning up the volume on a good track.
explanation.definitionFit: Listening is paying attention to sound, trying to catch it with the ears.

clue.text: Lively sparrow avoiding pointer with good reason

indicators.note: avoiding means leaving out, so those letters are dropped from sparrow

parts.note: an arrow is a pointer, as on a sign
rightly means justifiably, with good reason

explanation.surface: A lively little bird dodges a hunting dog, and sensibly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointer' looks like a gun dog, but it is an arrow. Remove ARROW from SPARROW to leave SP.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprightly means full of energy and briskness, spry and lively.

clue.text: Misrepresented Hercules and Pan as folkloric beings

indicators.note: misrepresented means shown in a false form, so the letters of the two names are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two mythological figures, a Greek hero and a goat god, are wrongly cast as creatures of folk tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Leprechauns are mischievous little men of Irish folklore, said to guard pots of gold.

clue.text: Pawn jewellery bringing in unknown one for valuing

parts.note: P is the chess abbreviation for pawn

indicators.note: bringing in means the word for jewellery takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a ring is a piece of jewellery
Z is a mathematical unknown, like x and y
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone pawns their jewellery, getting a single unknown sum for its worth.
explanation.definitionFit: Prizing something is valuing or treasuring it highly.

clue.text: You and I must leave Tower Hill

indicators.note: must leave means those letters are taken out of the word tower

parts.note: we is you and I together

explanation.surface: Two people are ordered off Tower Hill, the London site near the Tower.
explanation.walkthrough: Tower Hill is a real place in London, which disguises the definition 'Hill'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tor is a rocky peak or hilltop, especially on Dartmoor in south-west England.

clue.text: Reduce temperature with poultry, opening shed

parts.note: T is the symbol for temperature

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter; shed means that letter is dropped

parts.note: chicken is poultry

explanation.surface: A cook lowers the heat under the chicken while the garden shed is opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduce' is the cooking sense: boil a sauce down so it thickens.
explanation.definitionFit: In cooking, reducing a sauce by boiling makes it denser, so the two verbs coincide.

clue.text: Twist smart speaker's lead around

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its front, so its first letter
around means the word for smart is turned the other way

parts.note: to smart and to nip both mean to sting

explanation.surface: Someone twists the cable of a smart speaker round and round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart speaker' looks like a gadget, but 'smart' is a verb meaning sting, NIP turned backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin something is to turn or twirl it, as in giving a ball a twist.

clue.text: Cut down small hollow tree

indicators.note: a hollow word has had its insides removed, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: Someone fells a little tree that has gone hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: To slash prices or spending is to reduce them drastically.

clue.text: Exciting night catching Netherlands against Italy

indicators.note: catching means the word for night holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: evening is the night-time, a near synonym

indicators.note: against here means placed right next to, touching

parts.note: NL is the international code for the Netherlands
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A thrilling evening of football with the Dutch playing the Italians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Against' reads as a football fixture, but it only means the two country codes sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enlivening brings energy and excitement, making things lively.

clue.text: German's OK with unlimited Pils for jug

parts.note: ja is German for yes

indicators.note: without limits means the first and last letters are removed, keeping the middle

explanation.surface: A German approves of a jug of lager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jug' looks like a beer jug, but it is slang for prison. Pils is pilsner lager.
explanation.definitionFit: Jug is old slang for prison, so jail is a synonym.

clue.text: Park behind Shaun the Sheep, say

definitions.text: Park behind Shaun the Sheep, say

parts.words: Park behind Shaun the Sheep, say
parts.note: Nick Park, the British creator of Wallace and Gromit and Shaun the Sheep, makes clay figures move on screen

explanation.walkthrough: 'Park' looks like a place behind which a sheep might graze; it is Nick Park, the man behind the animated Shaun the Sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who creates animated films by bringing drawings or models to life is in that job.

clue.text: Permit husband to cut in dense shrubs

indicators.note: to cut means the letter for husband is cut out of the word

parts.note: a thicket is a dense growth of shrubs
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone gives a husband permission to trim back an overgrown hedge.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticket is a pass or permit allowing entry or travel.

clue.text: Tall tale about fine luxurious existence

parts.note: high means tall

indicators.note: about means the word for tale goes round the letter for fine

parts.note: a tale is a lie, a made-up story
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A tall story about living in style and comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tall tale' reads as one phrase, but the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The high life is a lavish style of living enjoyed by the rich and fashionable.

clue.text: Arranged change when getting year for hospital operation

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are put into a new order
getting a year for hospital means the letter for hospital is swapped out for another
for marks what is exchanged, the year in place of hospital

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A change is scheduled in the year a hospital operation was arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: CHANGE with its H swapped for Y gives CYANGE, which is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An agency is an organisation or business set up to act, as in an operation run on behalf of others.
